name: Blockade Ferris
specific_features: Ring of active volcanoes surrounding a central caldera basin, creating a natural blockade
description: Blockade Ferris is a volcanic world defined by a ring of massive shield volcanoes that encircle a central caldera basin three hundred kilometers across. This volcanic ring creates a natural blockade -- constant eruptions, pyroclastic flows, and toxic gas emissions make passage between the outer surface and the caldera interior effectively impossible by surface travel. The outer plains are scorched wastelands of cooling lava and sulfur crystal formations.

The atmosphere is a choking mixture of sulfur dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, and volcanic particulate, reducing visibility to meters during eruption cycles and permanently tinting the sky a sickly yellow-orange. Lightning storms generated by the ash clouds are continuous, their discharges painting the smoke-filled sky in jagged white. The heat is relentless, radiating from both the sun above and the magma below.

The central caldera basin, shielded from the worst volcanic activity by the encircling mountains, is paradoxically the most geologically stable region on the planet. Orbital imaging has revealed flat, cooled basalt floors and what appear to be mineral-rich hot springs within the basin. However, reaching the interior requires either orbital insertion directly into the caldera or tunneling through hundreds of kilometers of volcanically active rock.

Blockade Ferris has been classified as a geothermal energy reserve of exceptional potential, its volcanic output sufficient to power industrial operations on a sector-wide scale. The engineering challenge of harnessing that energy without being consumed by it remains unsolved. Several survey probes have been lost to eruptions during caldera descent attempts, and the planet has earned a reputation as a graveyard for ambitious engineering proposals.
